principles: One canonical owner per fact; matrices are derived views.
Structure is checked before implementation and executable evidence before REVIEW.
Hard gates consume typed, fresh, mechanically verifiable facts rather than prose.
Rollout must preserve legacy compatibility and provide actionable diagnostics.
drivers: Reduce REVIEW rounds caused by late discovery of missing proof obligations.
Reuse existing milestone ledger and ProofStory acceptance bindings.
Make the proposal precise enough for independent audit and later implementation.
Avoid claiming assurance that transcript or mutation evidence cannot support.

options.name: A: Extend ProofStory acceptanceBindings with nested verification topology
pros: Keeps claim ownership in the existing acceptance contract.
Allows milestone and verificationIntent totality checks to reuse current references.
cons: Requires careful versioning and legacy normalization.

options.name: B: Add a standalone acceptance_matrix artifact
pros: Easy to render and inspect independently.
Can be introduced without changing the acceptanceBindings shape immediately.
cons: Risks becoming an unaudited second gate truth source.

options.name: C: Keep schema unchanged and rely on reviewer prompts
pros: No schema migration or new commands.
cons: Repeats the B-407c late-discovery failure mode.
Prompt compliance cannot serve as gate evidence.

chosen: A: Extend ProofStory acceptanceBindings with nested verification topology
rationale: Option A places detailed verification obligations next to the acceptance claim they justify, while milestones continue to own intent totality and verificationIntent/evidence continue to own executable coverage. A rendered acceptance matrix remains useful but is computed from the canonical graph rather than persisted separately.

preMortem.scenario: The proposed topology duplicates milestone or verificationIntent semantics and creates conflicting owners.
preMortem.trigger: The schema repeats claims, doneMeans, or evidence status instead of referencing canonical IDs.
preMortem.consequence: Hosts cannot know which artifact controls lifecycle decisions, and updates drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Define a field-ownership table, reference-only topology edges, and reject duplicate inline claims in normalization.

preMortem.scenario: The pre-review gate accepts prose or command strings without proof that mutations bite.
preMortem.trigger: A populated topology is treated as sufficient even when no fresh receipt or expected failing mutation exists.
preMortem.consequence: REVIEW rounds fall but false assurance rises.
preMortem.mitigation: Separate PLAN structural admission from DEV executable evidence; require typed receipts, expected outcomes, authority, freshness, and mutation polarity.

preMortem.scenario: Enforcement blocks legacy or docs-only stories unexpectedly.
preMortem.trigger: New required fields are applied globally with no schema/version or risk-path distinction.
preMortem.consequence: Lifecycle adoption stalls and operators bypass the system.
preMortem.mitigation: Specify derived applicability, legacy normalization, docs-only exemptions, observe-warn-enforce rollout, and bite tests for each mode.

preMortem.scenario: The plan is mistaken for shipped behavior.
preMortem.trigger: Status language or examples omit Proposed labels and current-state boundaries.
preMortem.consequence: Auditors and hosts rely on gates that do not exist.
preMortem.mitigation: Add an explicit status banner, current-vs-target table, implementation waves, and a no-runtime-change acceptance criterion.
